Q: How to configure pytest for alembic migrations A:

First, let's initializing the alembic and configure itself. (I prefer to place migrations for a project in a folder with the same name.)

alembic init app/migrations

After... open alembic.ini check and edit the following lines:

# .....
script_location = %(here)s/app/migrations  # <--- should be with %(here)s

# .....
sqlalchemy.url = # <--- uncomment this line and set empty

After... open the env.py file, that will be located in the app/migrations folder, and add the following code:

# include the configuration from the FastAPI app
from app.core.config import get_settings
settings = get_settings()

'''
Here we set the dynamic database URL.
If we use tests, we will substitute the value we need into sqlalchemy.url
(more on this below).
'''
DATABASE_URL = config.get_main_option('sqlalchemy.url') or settings.ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL

If we work with our application, then the ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL specified in our configuration file will be automatically taken.

This completes the alembic settings!

Now open .env file your project and add into some as:

ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg2://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/your_db
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@127.0.0.1:5434/test_db # 'sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:'

I deploy two postgres databases in Podman based on a single image of postgres version 18. For the main database, I specified port 5432 on the local machine and in the container (default postgres port). For the test database, I set the connection port to 5434, and in the container also left, the port 5432, as the containers are isolated from each other.

Here's an important! Alembic doesn't support asynchronous connections, so we use the psycopg2 adapter for standard migrations. The application must run asynchrone with database. For tests to run correctly, they must also run asynchronously. That's why, we use the asyncpg adapter for both the main and test databases.

Now, to run the tests, we need to create them and configure them. To do this, create the following structure in the project folder:

+---tests
|   |   conftest.py
|   |   pytest.ini
|   |   __init__.py
|   |
|   +---integration
|   |   \---crud
|   |       |   test_<name>.py
|   |
|   +---unit
|   |   \---services

Add the following code to conftest.py:

import pytest_asyncio

from typing import AsyncGenerator

from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

from app.core.config import get_settings

settings = get_settings()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope='session')
async def engine() -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncEngine, None]:
    # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncEngine
    engine = create_async_engine(settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL, echo=False, poolclass=NullPool)
    yield engine
    await engine.dispose()


async def async_session(engine: AsyncEngine) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]:
    # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.async_sessionmaker
    async with async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)() as session:
        await session.begin()
        try:
            yield session
        finally:
            await session.rollback()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope='session', autouse=True)
async def apply_migrations(engine: AsyncEngine) -> None:
    alembic_cfg = Config('alembic.ini')
    alembic_cfg.set_main_option('sqlalchemy.url', settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL)

    async with engine.connect() as connect:
        try:
            await connect.run_sync(lambda connection: command.upgrade(alembic_cfg, 'head'))
            # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncConnection.run_sync
            # await connect.run_sync(lambda sync_conn: command.downgrade(alembic_cfg, 'base'))  # optional
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error applying migrations: {e}")
            raise
        finally:
            await connect.rollback()

Explanations:

  • Each test started with a clean database. All changes made during the test disappeared after its completion. Even if the test failed mid-run, the database didn't remain "dirty."

    with session.begin()

  • Replace the database URL. Since SQLAlchemy hide the password when outputting the URL, we explicitly use the database URL from .env, and not, for example, from engine.url, i.e., we essentially transfer raw data:

    alembic_cfg.set_main_option('sqlalchemy.url', settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL)

Important!

  • Use run_sync for synchronous migrations, since Alembic itself is not asynchronous.

  • Create one asynchronous engine for the entire test session using parameter scope='session' of fixture.

  • Create an asynchronous SQLAlchemy session for each test a fixture as function, as tests must be isolated so that changes to the database in one test do not affect others.

    If you set scope='session', all tests will use the same session object, which can lead to conflicts.

  • Since migrations need to be run once for the entire test session, and not before each test and for automatically upgrade migrations before tests, also using the scope='session' for fixture and option autouse=True.

  • For the migration fixture to run, there must be at least one active integration test associated with the database!

As a result, running the pytest test command will now automatically apply migrations to the database.

Also, when running migrations in the normal Alembic mode, the migrations will be applied to the main database without affecting the test database.

Tested on: alembic==1.17.2, fastapi==0.124.0, pytest==9.0.2, SQLAlchemy==2.0.44, PG_VERSION=18.0-1.pgdg13+3 (Podman systemd units)

Q: Statement contains an OUTPUT clause without INTO clause error A:

I think it may be related to what Anthony Horne wrote.

Does this work?

ALTER TRIGGER [dbo].[Trigger_RootIdUpdate] 
  ON  [dbo].[Messages] 
  AFTER INSERT
AS BEGIN
  UPDATE 
    Messages
  SET 
    Messages.RootId = INSERTED.MessageId 
  FROM Messages Msg
  JOIN INSERTED ON 
    Msg.MessageId = INSERTED.MessageId 
  WHERE 
    Msg.MessageId = INSERTED.MessageId 
    AND INSERTED.RootId = 0;
END

Q: Is it possible to register a model in MLflow model registry without pickling the model? A:

Any flavour of mlflow.pyfunc.log_model uses only pickle, cloudpickle or skops for serialization format (as of 3.13.0). Since you can reproduce your model using state_dict you can just log it the following way:

import mlflow


with mlflow.start_run() as run:
    mlflow.log_dict(state_dict, artifact_file="model_state.pth")
    # in your case you are using .log_artifact, nothing is logged, since you do not pass the dictionary, only the path for it on the remote server
    run_id = run.info.run_id

model_uri = f"runs:/{run_id}/model"
mlflow.register_model(model_uri, "Test") # now, the Test model will appear in the model registry

To retrieve it, suppose you want to access the latest version of your model:

from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient


client = MlflowClient()
model_versions = client.search_model_versions("name='Test'")
latest = max(model_versions, key=lambda v: int(v.version))
mlflow_model_state_path = client.download_artifacts(run_id=latest.run_id, path="model/model_state.pth")
# After you have successfully downloaded the file, you need to initialize the model with model_state; the logic varies across different APIs

Q: Is it possible to change a part of the background color of an image, when the image is a table? A:

I have 3 possible ways from an image-analysis perspective

Splitting You can split the images in two part. First part is just your normal flow (load image, detect text on it). The second flow you first take the negative of the image (255 - img) and than detect text.

The two results will need to be merged afterwards.

difference filter You can first apply a difference filter/edge detection this will high everything with a high contrast BUT can alter the shape of the letters if done to extreme or if some letters are way bigger.

contour finding + filling Again an edge detection but now very thin and followed with an contour detection. This will redraw all letter in one color.

Q: OpenCV 3.1.0: Save and load trained SVMs A:

After searching for a while I found out that if I use a linear kernel there is no problem at all. So then I can save and load the SVM and the prediction is correct. So I started to search for a reason why it works for the linear kernel and not for the other kernels.

The answer is that there is a bug in OpenCV 3.1 according to issue #5054 on Github. I tried the proposed solution but it still didn't work. Eventually I donwloaded OpenCV 2.4 and now everything works well.

Q: How can I efficiently delete expired records in PostgreSQL? A:

I would not recommend using partitioning. Read the Limitations part of the partitioning documentation:

  • To create a unique or primary key constraint on a partitioned table, the partition keys must not include any expressions or function calls and the constraint's columns must include all of the partition key columns. This limitation exists because the individual indexes making up the constraint can only directly enforce uniqueness within their own partitions; therefore, the partition structure itself must guarantee that there are not duplicates in different partitions.

For example, if you try to partition your table by expires_at, and assuming id is meant to be the primary key, you immediately get this error when you try to create the table.

CREATE TABLE omebox_table (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  expires_at TIMESTAMP
) PARTITION BY RANGE(expires_at);

ERROR:  unique constraint on partitioned table must include all partitioning columns
DETAIL:  PRIMARY KEY constraint on table "omebox_table" lacks column "expires_at" 
which is part of the partition key.

Even if you could create such a table (for example by giving it no primary key constraint—I don't recommend this), a partitioned table will complicate optimization of queries that do not filter by expires_at.

I would guess that deleting records is not the query you most need to optimize in this table. There are other queries you would also like to be optimized.

What I suggest is to use a scheduled job, in which you delete rows in fixed-size batches.

Pseudocode:

while True:
  start transaction
    DELETE FROM omebox_table 
    WHERE expires_at < current_timestamp - interval '7 days' 
    LIMIT 1000;
  commit transaction

  check the number of rows deleted.
  if the number is zero:
    break out of the loop
  
end while loop

Using fixed-size batches helps to prevent any one transaction from modifying an unbounded number of rows (the number 1000 I show is not special, it's just an example).

This strategy should be adequate for a long time. Someday if your service is used very heavily, you might reach a volume where it takes too long to delete rows using this solution. But at that point, you must have many other scaling issues and you need to reconsider many parts of your application architecture.
